question.text: Depository receipts (DRs) are financial instruments that:

answer.text: Represent shares of a local company but are listed and traded on a stock exchange outside the country, issued in foreign currency
Are receipts issued by depositories for holding physical gold
Are fixed deposit receipts issued by foreign banks to Indian investors
Are government bonds traded exclusively on the domestic market

explanation.text: The Logic: Depository receipts are financial instruments that represent shares of a local company but are listed and traded on a stock exchange outside the country, and are issued in foreign currency. ADRs are the variant listed in the United States, while GDRs are listed on exchanges outside the US. The Trap: Option B confuses DRs with Electronic Gold Receipts. Option C describes bank fixed deposits, not depository receipts. Option D describes domestic government bonds. Note: Hold on to the three-part DR definition: local-company shares, foreign-listed, foreign-currency issuance.
